page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the n1 server family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon core running at 2.3 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 13.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 6.5 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and operates on the x86_64 architecture with a 45 MB L3 cache.

Benchmark evaluations place the n1-highmem-2 in the lower performance tiers. Its single-core CPU performance is weak, scoring 1105.58 in stress-ng and 944.0 in Geekbench. Multi-core performance is poor, with a stress-ng score of 1452.88 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 1124.0. Memory bandwidth is also limited, recording 13.32 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 11.13 GB/sec for write operations. Database and web serving capabilities are modest, with Redis SET operations executing at 1.38 million operations per second and static web serving throughput reaching 1.58 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-highmem-2 provides a low-cost entry point for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high compute density. The trade-off is characterized by low processing throughput and constrained memory bandwidth in exchange for a larger memory allocation per vCPU. This profile makes the instance suitable for small-scale databases, caching layers, lightweight web serving, and basic memory-bound utility tasks rather than intensive computational or large-scale data processing workloads.
